findings.issue: sqlc code was never regenerated for query/fiado.sql: internal/db/fiado.sql.go does not exist, so db.GetCustomerByUserIDAndIDParams, db.ListPendingFiadoSalesByCustomerParams/Row and db.SummarizePendingFiadoSalesByCustomerParams/Row are undefined. 'go build ./...' in packages/api-go fails with 8 undefined errors and 'make test' cannot compile. AGENTS.md requires running 'make -C packages/api-go sqlc' after touching query/ or db/schema.sql.

Both queries LEFT JOIN an unfiltered grouped subquery 'SELECT sale_id, SUM(amount) FROM payments GROUP BY sale_id'. Postgres cannot push the s.user_id/s.customer_id quals into a non-LATERAL grouped subquery, so every request aggregates the entire payments table (all tenants) twice - once for the list, once for the summary - despite payments_sale_id_idx existing. Rewrite as a correlated/LATERAL subquery or join payments directly and GROUP BY s.id.

internalError() builds a brand-new AppError and discards the underlying store error: it is never wrapped with %w and never logged, and handler.writeFiadoFailure does not log either. A Postgres outage or malformed query on GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/fiado returns 500 with zero trace anywhere in the logs. AGENTS.md: return errors from lower layers, log at handler boundaries, wrap inspectable errors with %w.

The comment 'Same customer id must not match another users sales' promises tenant isolation coverage, but seedSale always inserts with userID/customerID and no sale is ever created for otherUserID/otherCustomerID. The 's.user_id = $1' filter in ListPendingFiadoSalesByCustomer and SummarizePendingFiadoSalesByCustomer is therefore never exercised; the 'no open sales' subtest passes trivially because that user has no rows at all. Dropping the user_id predicate would keep every assertion green.

The non-AppError fallback branch (generic error -> 500 with message 'Erro ao buscar fiado do cliente') is never exercised: TestCustomerFiado_serviceFailureIs500 injects an apperror.AppError, which takes the errors.As path. A plain error returned by a future lister implementation would hit untested code.

The summary (COUNT/SUM) and the page rows are read in two separate queries outside any transaction or repeatable-read snapshot. A payment settling a sale between the two reads makes pagination.total/total_pages and total_devido disagree with the returned data, and OFFSET-based paging can skip or duplicate sales for a client walking pages while payments are recorded.

numericFloat swallows Float64Value errors and NULL and returns 0. A numeric that fails conversion turns a real outstanding balance into saldo/total_devido of 0.00 in the JSON response - a silently wrong debt shown to the operator instead of an error. No test covers the error branch.

'saleDate, _ := timestamptzTime(row.SaleDate)' discards the validity flag, so an invalid/NULL sale_date is serialized as 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z in the 'data' field instead of being reported or omitted. The bool return of timestamptzTime is dead at its only call site.

Adding the broad prefix '/api/v1/customers/' to bearerRoutePrefixes exempts every current and future route under that prefix from the X-API-Key check whenever any Authorization: Bearer header is present (the API-key middleware only checks the prefix string, not token validity). Future non-bearer routes mounted under /api/v1/customers/ silently lose API-key enforcement.

The new 'fiado without bearer requires API key' case sets only wantStatus and omits wantCode, so assertJSONError is skipped and the UNAUTHORIZED error code/body is never asserted - unlike the sibling 'missing header'/'invalid header' cases which do assert it.

Only the 401 status is asserted; the test does not check that the stub lister was never invoked, nor the error body/code. It would still pass if the handler ran the query before the bearer middleware rejected the request.

Page exports Number and Limit, so callers can build one without NewPage (the tests already do: fiado.Page{Number: 3, Limit: 20}). Offset() then computes int32((Number-1)*Limit) with no bound check, silently wrapping to a negative OFFSET for large literals, which Postgres rejects at runtime. The MaxPage invariant is only enforced on the NewPage path.
